title: Grain Desk Standing Rule: Which Charges Are Drawn Onto the Money Released
content:
Which charges are drawn onto the money released on a statement under Grain Marketing Contracts turns on where the contract stands in its life.

**1.** Where the contract stands in delivering, every charge standing on the contract's grain ledger is drawn, whether it names the statement or not, because the desk clears the ledger each time it pays a live contract out.

**2.** Where the contract stands in fully delivered or in settled standing, the charge lines naming the statement are drawn together with the roll charges standing on the contract.

**3.** Where neither of those holds, only the charge lines naming the statement are drawn.

## The three standings side by side

| The contract stands in | What is drawn |
|---|---|
| delivering | every charge standing on the contract's grain ledger, named on the statement or not |
| fully delivered | the charge lines naming the statement, together with the roll charges standing on the contract |
| settled | the charge lines naming the statement, together with the roll charges standing on the contract |
| any other standing | only the charge lines naming the statement |

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A contract's grain ledger carries charge lines of 400.00 and 250.00 naming the statement, a further charge line of 180.00 naming an earlier statement, and roll charges of 320.00. Standing in delivering, the charges drawn come to 1,150.00. Standing in fully delivered, they come to 970.00. Standing in any other way, they come to 650.00.
